display_name: Shahu I, Chhatrapati of the Marathas
one_line: Early 18th‑century Maratha sovereign overseeing revenue officers and the fiscal-military state.

appearance.age_look: Looks late 30s to early 40s, solid medium-tall build, with a calm but commanding posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with warm medium-brown Deccan complexion, slightly prominent nose, well-kept moustache curving gently down, soft but sharp dark eyes with thick brows; default expression is composed and thoughtful, often with a faint, reassuring half‑smile.
appearance.hair: Black hair tied back in a low knot under a traditional Maratha turban (pheta) wrapped in deep saffron cloth with a subtle gold border, slightly angled to the right with a small fabric tail at the back.
appearance.costume: He wears an early-18th-century Maratha royal angarkha in off‑white fine cotton with a subtle vertical weave, knee-length and overlapping to the right, edged with narrow gold piping; over this a sleeveless deep red silk waistcoat-like jhabba, slightly shorter than the angarkha, with simple round metal buttons; his lower garment is a white cotton dhoti wrapped in the Marathi style, pleated in front, falling to the ankles and bordered with a thin red stripe; around his waist is a broad dark-green cotton sash (patka) with woven gold thread at the ends, tied to the left with one end hanging; he wears soft brown leather mojari shoes with slightly upturned toes; jewellery is restrained but royal—small gold hoop earrings, a simple gold chain with a single round pendant, and a modest string of white beads close to the neck; on his right wrist a plain gold bangle, and on his left a thin red-and-gold sacred thread bracelet; his outfit has no fantasy ornament but shows neat, practical tailoring suitable for court and field inspections.
appearance.signature: In his left hand he holds a rolled palm-leaf revenue register tied with a red cord, while at his left hip a sheathed straight-bladed talwar with a simple steel hilt and plain brown leather scabbard hangs from his green waist sash—he often gestures with the register when addressing officers.

ref_desc: Shahu I is a medium‑tall, warm-brown Maratha king with an oval face, black hair in a low knot under a saffron pheta, wearing an off‑white angarkha, deep red sleeveless jhabba, white dhoti, dark‑green waist sash, brown mojari shoes, simple gold jewellery, and carrying a rolled palm‑leaf revenue register with a sheathed talwar at his hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Shahu I, early 18th‑century Maratha sovereign, standing in a dignified pose: a medium‑tall, solidly built man with a warm medium‑brown complexion, oval face, thoughtful dark eyes, thick brows, a well-kept downward moustache, and black hair tied in a low knot under a traditional Maratha pheta turban wrapped in deep saffron cloth with a narrow gold border and a small fabric tail at the back. Show him in an off‑white fine cotton angarkha, knee-length, overlapping to the right with narrow gold piping, worn under a sleeveless deep red silk jhabba that is slightly shorter and fastened with simple round metal buttons. His lower garment is a white cotton dhoti in Marathi style, pleated in front, reaching the ankles with a thin red border, and around his waist is a broad dark‑green cotton sash (patka) with woven gold thread ends tied on the left, one end hanging down. At his feet are soft brown leather mojari shoes with gently upturned toes. Add restrained royal jewellery: small gold hoop earrings, a simple gold chain with a single round pendant, a short string of white beads at the neck, a plain gold bangle on the right wrist, and a thin red‑and‑gold sacred thread bracelet on the left. His signature items are a rolled palm‑leaf revenue register tied with a red cord held in his left hand, and a sheathed straight-bladed talwar with a simple steel hilt and plain brown leather scabbard hanging from his green sash at the left hip. Use a palette dominated by deep red, off‑white, saffron, dark green, and brown leather, and present him from multiple angles to clearly show his face, turban, garments, sash, footwear, and the way the register and sword are carried.
